chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Music Town's songwriting service and arts center
summary: They advertised in the Chicago Defender and Pittsburgh Courier, wrote and recorded songs on a small disc machine, and aimed for drama and dance as well.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And at Music Town--this is where you had your songwriting service, right?
And you told me about all the mail you got and all the work you did there writing songs for people, uh, and recording them. Where did you advertise? You said you had mail from all over the...
I advertised in the Chicago Defender and the, uh, ...what's that Pittsburgh thing?
Courier. See? And they would go everywhere.
Right. They were sold in all the cities.

Then. And I used to get calls, you know, writing from all over the United States nearly. We had a little recording machine about as big as this, and we could make a disc on it, and, naturally, Austin would play the record, and I'd straighten out the lyrics and everything, and we'd get together on the tune, and he'd write it, and we'd record it, and, if they wanted a little band, we'd get a guita...a couple of guitars or something and a singer and... whatever they wanted. We'd make it and send it to 'em.
And so you had just about all of the arts represented at Music Town. You had drama and dance and...
That's what we wanted to have, yeah.
Well, what? It didn't work out that way?
Oh, yeah, we had 'em for awhile. You know, the war broke up things...
